newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Calmer Caracas stocks close up as CANTV recovers.
newsitem.headline: Calmer Caracas stocks close up as CANTV recovers.

text.p: Caracas stocks closed higher in moderate trade, lead by a recovery in telephone company CANTV, as Venezuelan shares prices bounced back from a week-long sell-off, traders said.
"The market was reacting, correcting ... recent falls have been very big, especially in CANTV," said Cavelba broker Rafael Alcantara.
Traders said CANTV was now the most attractively priced telecom stock in the region.
"It's logical that CANTV stock should rise, especially after yesterday's sell-off," said one.

As workers began an indefinite strike today, CANTV traded up 130.00 bolivars to 1975.00 after slumping nearly 20 percent in the past two weeks on concern over strikes and a delay in second quarter rate increases. The share was boosted by a Credit Lyonnais buy recommendation.

In the wider market, the bolsa's 19-share .IBC index rose 0.62 percent to close at 6,099.33 points as 23 million shares traded, worth 3.5 billion bolivars ($7.3 million), according to preliminary figures from the exchange.
Merinvest's composite .MRCP index, which includes CANTV, gained 2.17 percent to close at 93.99 points.
Among traded issues, 13 rose, 12 fell and 12 closed flat.
Traders said they saw calmer sessions continuing for the rest of the week, with the market watching for news from the government on CANTV rate increases.
